Changelog

What's new

Every release, newest first. Follow along with the releases feed, or Watch → Custom → Releases on GitHub. Older versions are on the releases page.

0.7.713 October 2026

Notes

  • Save as note on a screenshot or image that text recognition has not reached yet now waits for it and then writes the note, instead of failing with "nothing to write".
0.7.611 October 2026

Calendar

  • The panel's Add to calendar button now honours the suggestions setting: while event suggestions are on, pressing it (or the c key) opens the same Add / Edit… / Not Now review the suggestion banner offers — you see the title, day and place MemoryClip detected before anything is written.
  • Every manual add now posts the created-event notification carrying Open in Calendar — which lands on the event's own day — and Undo, so "added" is never something you have to take on faith.
  • Detection understands labelled invitation layouts: a clock time on its own TIME: row is now joined to the date instead of producing an all-day event, and section headers like "EVENT DETAILS" or bare DATE: labels can no longer become the event's title.
  • Offer and confirmation banners now show the detected location, so a wrong venue is visible before and after the event is added.

Build hardening

  • Scripts/verify_app.sh fails the app build if a module resource bundle the code needs is missing from the package — the class of bug that crashed the Shortcuts settings pane.
  • publish_release.sh now ends a release on its notes commit rather than on the Homebrew cask bump, and refuses a release whose notes file is missing or already committed.
0.7.510 October 2026

What's new

  • Settings → Shortcuts opens instead of crashing. A resource bundle the app has always needed was never copied into the .app — this was a latent crash in every release, and it is finally gone.
  • The missing-language callout can be dismissed. The "already read a screenshot in X" banner now offers Dismiss: the listed languages will not re-announce themselves on every screenshot, unless you tick one — that is you saying you want it after all.
  • Privacy hardening from an app-wide audit. Secret clips are now invisible to Shortcuts and Spotlight answers (existence and source app included — they never carried plaintext). Silent store writes from the panel now log instead of vanishing, a drag-time race is closed, and secret persistence failures report instead of passing in silence.
0.7.38 October 2026

What's new

  • Detected appointments ask before writing. A clip that looks like an event now offers it instead of saving — Add creates it, Edit… opens a draft in Calendar for tweaking first, Not Now leaves it alone. Tapping the offer banner raises the same three choices as a dialog.
  • The "Added to your calendar" banner opens the event's day. Tapping it — or its Open button — lands Calendar on the date the event landed on, and Undo still retracts the creation it announced.
  • Clipboard reliability hardening: an edit made while OCR, translation, thumbnail or note work is still in flight can no longer be overwritten by the stale write-back, and the local store migration survives a permissions hiccup without losing history.
  • The release bundle builds on the current Swift toolchain again.
0.7.26 October 2026

What's new

  • Long preview text wraps at the edge of the pane. Lines no longer run past it, in either tab, for text and screenshot clips.
  • The hint bubbles float in the top bar, above the clips, and fade after 7 seconds.
  • The release bundle builds with the newest Swift toolchain.
0.7.15 October 2026

What's new

  • The original text stays in the preview while it's translated. The text under a screenshot has two tabs, Original and the translation, and ⌘T switches between them.
  • The preview no longer jumps while a translation streams in.
  • Tables show as grids in the translation too.
  • An article beside a sidebar is no longer read as a two-column table.
  • The Quick Look hint sits at the top of the preview, off the text.
0.7.03 October 2026

What's new

  • Passwords and API keys are encrypted with the Secure Enclave. Copied private keys, tokens (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, Slack, Stripe), JWTs, connection strings and one-time codes show as a label and a mask. Touch ID reveals one for 30 seconds, and the clipboard clears 90 seconds after a paste. Settings › Privacy can drop them or keep them as plain text instead.
  • Pinboards. Group pinned clips into named, ordered boards shown as chips under the search bar. ⌘P files a clip, ⌃1-9 jumps to a board, ⌥⇧← → reorders within it. Your existing pins are in Pinned.
  • Search operators: app:, type:, is:pinned, is:secret, in:<board>, after:7d, before:, on:. Prefix - to exclude. Type ? for the list.
  • Edit a clip before pasting it. ⌘I opens the editor, ⌘S saves, ⌘Return saves and pastes, ⌘Z restores the original.
  • Shortcuts and Spotlight: Get Latest Clip, Search Clips, Copy Clip and Open MemoryClip.
  • History keeps 5,000 clips for 90 days by default. Pick a limit from 200 to Unlimited, or keep clips for a year. Settings shows the disk space used, and lowering a limit says how many clips it will delete first. Limits you set yourself are kept.
  • The welcome tour lets you record your own panel shortcut if another app already uses ⇧⌘V.
  • The OCR switch lives in one place, under Settings › Panel.
0.6.118 September 2026

What's new

  • ⌘Y opens the preview while searching. Type a query, pick a card with ↑ ↓, press ⌘Y. Space still types into the search field.
  • The panel reopens on the newest clip, not wherever you last scrolled.
  • More tracking parameters removed: Instagram stkn, Threads, Twitch, Snapchat, Etsy, Walmart, IMDb, Netflix and Google, plus extra TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, Amazon, Spotify and Reddit share tags.
0.6.030 August 2026

What's new

  • Copied links are stripped of tracking parameters. ?igsh=, utm_*, fbclid, si, Amazon ref_, and per-site rules for Instagram, YouTube, X, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, Spotify, Reddit, eBay and AliExpress. Paste is clean everywhere, not just from the panel.
  • ⌘C copies your selection in the preview pane. Select a few words and copy them, instead of right-clicking for the whole clip.
  • Use original gives the untouched URL back from any cleaned clip, and a Cleaned badge marks them.
  • New Links settings under Privacy: turn cleaning off, keep utm_*, or exclude specific sites. Links carrying a token, code or signature are never touched.
  • Clean Link transform for links captured before this release.
  • The footer counts every match in the store, not just the loaded page.
  • The hint bubble is readable over any card, in both appearances.
0.5.222 August 2026

What's new

  • The disk image says to quit MemoryClip first. Taking an update opens the new version's disk image while the old one is still running, and macOS will not replace an app mid-flight — so the drag onto Applications failed with nothing on screen to explain it. The window now carries the instruction, and where to find Quit, laid out along the drag itself.
0.5.121 August 2026

What's new

  • The window that opens after an update now offers to tell you about the next one. macOS drops an ad-hoc signed app's permissions every time it is replaced, so MemoryClip already opens a window after an update to ask for them back — which means it opens for exactly the people who installed by hand. The daily update check is offered there too, still off by default and still something that never installs anything itself.
0.5.021 August 2026

What's new

  • The panel says which keys it answers to. Search for a clip and a bubble over the deck names the keys that walk the matches; select several and it says what Return will paste; open the preview on a picture or a file and it says that Space goes to Quick Look. Each one goes as soon as you use the key it names.
  • Tell me when there is a new version — Settings → General → Updates, and a page of the first-run tour. Off by default, and the only network call MemoryClip can make. On, it asks GitHub once a day what the newest release is, sending nothing about you; when there is one you get a single notification, and taking it downloads that release and opens the disk image for the same drag as the first install. It never installs anything itself.
  • Search understands a sentence. Type "that error about the deploy failing" and it finds the clip that says deployment to production failed. Every word has to match rather than the whole phrase being looked for verbatim, and words are reduced to the stem they share with their dictionary form. Search now also covers what the on-device model wrote about a clip — its summary, title and tags — and both translations.
  • Drag a clip out of the panel into any app. A screenshot travels as the file it already is, never as a copy of its bytes.
  • Select several clips at once. ⇧-click and ⇧↑/↓ extend, ⌘-click picks clips out one at a time, and Return pastes the lot in order. Vim mode gains v.
  • Import your history back. Settings → History → Import… reads a JSON export, keeping the times clips were first copied and skipping any already there, so moving to a new Mac keeps the history.
  • Never capture from apps you name. Settings → Privacy → Excluded apps. Nothing copied there reaches the store at all, and unlike the built-in password-manager list it keeps applying with sensitive-content filtering off.
  • Always paste as plain text into apps you name. Settings → General → Pasting, seeded with the usual terminals and editors, every entry removable.
  • Fourteen more transforms, and the menu is grouped: Case, JSON, Encoding, Color, Time and Lines. Colours convert between hex, rgb() and hsl(), and a Unix timestamp becomes a date and back.
  • Notes translate into the language you choose, not always English — Settings → Translation → Language, which now governs notes and the panel's preview alike. Existing installs keep English until a language is picked.
